brief: 5 things the skincare industry doesn't want you to know.

slots.headline: Why Your Shelf Lies?
slots.subtitle: Five secrets the industry hopes you never google.

slots.title: Price Is Just Marketing
slots.body: That hundred-dollar cream shares the same base as drugstore tubs. You're paying for fragrance and glass, not results. Simple formulas often outperform luxury hype.

slots.title: Over-Exfoliation Sells More Product
slots.body: Burning means it's working? That's a myth invented to sell serums. Stripping your barrier creates problems that need more bottles. Gentle routines build real resilience.

slots.title: Clean Beauty Is Unregulated
slots.body: Terms like 'clean' and 'non-toxic' have zero legal meaning. Anyone can slap them on a label. Marketing teams know green fonts feel safer than chemistry.

slots.title: You Need Fewer Steps
slots.body: The famous ten-step routine was born from retail strategy, not dermatology. More layers equal more shelf space and repeat purchases. Skin prefers consistency over clutter.

slots.title: SPF Makeup Is Not Enough
slots.body: That foundation claims SPF thirty, but you never apply a teaspoon of it. Real protection requires dedicated sunscreen applied generously. Makeup is decoration, not defense.

slots.title: Trust Your Skin More
slots.body: The industry profits on insecurity and overcomplicated shelves. Start with cleanser, moisturizer, and sunscreen. Everything else is optional until you truly need it.
